newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices limp late, grades steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices limp late, grades steady.

text.p: A combination of sagging prompt refinery demand and a lack of interested players kept U.S. domestic crude markets quiet on Wednesday, leaving the cash markets lacking in sustainable direction.

Traders said an industry gathering in Dallas this evening had depleted volumes all session. Evidence of lackluster sales could be seen from stagnant grade differentials and the sheer absence of confirmed trades.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late at $20.15-25 a barrel, around 20-25 cents lower than late Tuesday. June/July spreads were virtually even all session.
